headline: EU Regulatory Update: Green Claims, Right to Repair, and CSRD Scope
summary: Reports indicate the EU Commission plans to scrap the Green Claims Directive, while the Right to Repair law has entered into force. Legal analysis confirms your business remains in scope for CSRD reporting from 2027, but outside direct CSDDD duties. Public consultations on product repairability are also underway.

items.title: Commission reportedly moves to scrap proposed Green Claims Directive
items.what: Media reports indicate the European Commission intends to withdraw the proposed Green Claims Directive, potentially dropping mandatory third-party verification for environmental claims.
items.meaning: Though not yet official law, withdrawal would simplify marketing claims for your tools and packaging, though general anti-greenwashing rules still apply.
items.action: Monitor official Commission updates before modifying internal environmental claim review processes.

sources.title: EU Pulls Plug on Green Claims Directive
Commission confirms plans to scrap Green Claims Directive
Independent verification for greenwashing claims officially dropped by EU Commission

items.title: Right to Repair rules take effect as new consultation opens
items.what: The Right to Repair Directive took effect on 1 November 2026, while the Commission launched a public consultation on further strengthening product repairability.
items.meaning: Directly affects your consumer power tools and garden equipment. You must ensure spare parts availability, repair access, and product serviceability.
items.action: Review spare parts supply chains with Chinese manufacturers to ensure compliance with repair standards.

sources.title: New Law on Right to Repair Takes Effect
Commission launches public consultation on making products easier to repair

items.title: Omnibus analysis details CSRD inclusion and CSDDD exclusion
items.what: Recent legal analysis details how Omnibus reforms adjust corporate sustainability reporting while setting higher thresholds for corporate due diligence.
items.meaning: With over 1,000 employees and €450m turnover, your company is in scope for CSRD starting FY 2027, but remains exempt from direct CSDDD duties.
items.action: Focus supplier sustainability data collection on CSRD reporting alignment rather than full CSDDD mapping.
